Spinel Leviathan Syndara 
PORTAL REDIRECTION 
Portal Redirection is one of Syndara’s strongest 
abilities, since it automatically redirects attacks.  
When used effectively, it can turn ranged 
attackers, especially ranged attackers who typically 
make only one attack per round, into 
disadvantages to the PCs, which is incredibly 
frustrating in the final fight of the campaign. If 
you have one or more ranged PCs, consider 
changing portal redirection so that it can be used 
on both ranged and melee attacks, but only on 
missed attacks.  If the PCs learn how this ability 
works, this also encourages them to play more 
cooperatively, to avoid having their most powerful 
attacks redirected. 
     On a related note, Spinel Leviathan Syndara 
has 3 different reactions, but only 1 reaction per 
round to use them with. If you have more than 4 
PCs and are adjusting the adventure accordingly, 
consider giving him additional reactions (such as 1 
reaction per enemy turn) rather than increasing his 
statistics or adding creatures.

NEW TEAMS 
This section contains 13 additional teams to complete the 32 teams initially present on danger island at the start of the 
adventure path. Each is presented on a specific recommended day to provide the most appropriate level of challenge to 
the PCs, though they can also be used outside of these days or as background characters that the PCs see or meet when 
they arrive on the island, or that they see fighting other teams.  
DAY 1 
HALLOWED GUARDIANS 
A group of young guardian nagas, this team has come to believe that 
their place is not in Nagajor, as all of the most sacred sites in that 
nation are already watched over by older nagas. They sought entry in 
the Ruby Phoenix Tournament as a way to learn about and experience 
the rest of the world, and frequently ask other teams about their 
homelands and the places they have been.  
GUARDIAN NAGA (4) 
 
 
 
        CREATURE 10 
In a fight, the Keepers stick together until they are repeatedly hit with 
area damage. Unless clearly outmatched at range, they hang back and 
use their ranged or support spells and spit, waiting for their 
opponents to come to them. Once engaged in melee, they encircle 
and flank a particular opponent and focus on them, though they take 
care not to kill anyone with their venom, using spells if necessary.  
 
ROVING RADIANCE 
These two lovers have made quite the name for themselves as 
wandering heroes in Minata. Devout followers of Desna, they have 
travelled across the nearly entire archipelago, and will now travel 
further, should they succeed in the qualifying round. They see the 
Ruby Phoenix Tournament, and Bonmu, one of the last islands they 
have yet to visit, as a way to test themselves to see if they are ready to 
face the wider world.

         CREATURE 12 
Weak Ki Adept; replace Monk Focus Spells 
Cleric Focus Spells DC 30, attack +23, (3 Focus Points); 7th agile feet, bit of luck, lucky 
break, moonbeam, touch of the moon, traveler’s transit 
This team stays mobile but close together so Kaleo can protect Cahya 
with Liberating Step. Cayha uses his speed, reach & focus spells to 
stay out of Kaleo’s way and avoid enemies, while harrying foes with 
Flurry of Blows or Knocking Sweep. Kaleo sometimes uses his free 
hand to Grapple prone foes, pinning them to the ground.  
ENCOUNTER BALANCE 
Assuming the PCs are level 12 on day 
1, level 13 on day 2, and level 14 on 
day 3, each of these teams should be a 
Moderate difficulty encounter. If your 
players are okay with it, feel free to 
ignore these guidelines! Facing 
opponents stronger than the PCs can 
help Danger Island feel like a living, 
unpredictable place rather than one 
that revolves around the player 
characters.

SOARING SOVEREIGNTY 
This unusual team hailing from the once-flying 
Shory city of Yjae consists of a single aeromancer 
named Karabo and two conjured air 
elementals. Karabo is something of a political 
dissident in Yjae, as they believe the best way to 
save the city from the extradimensional monsters 
that threaten it is to seek aid from the outside 
world, and so has entered the tournament to seek 
out powerful combatants and treasures that can 
aid them. 
KARABO 
 
 
    CREATURE 13 
Mage of Many Styles 
Aeromancer Karabo has mastered spells of flight as if they 
were mere cantrips and can cast 4th-level fly at will. Replace fly 
in their prepared spells with blazing dive at 4th-level.  
STORM LORD (2) 
 
      CREATURE 9 
If the enforcers will let them (GM’s discretion), 
Soaring Sovereignty begins a fight airborne, and 
ideally avoid melee combat entirely. The air 
elementals move to interpose themselves between 
Karabo and any ranged attackers or airborne 
enemies. For their part, Karabo focuses their 
spells on whichever foe seems best able to deal 
with flying combatants, whether that is an archer, 
another spellcaster, or a flying melee combatant.  
 
THUNDERING TIDE 
From the underwater nation of Xidao comes this 
pair of aquatic warriors. Though they know that 
they are unlikely to be able to win a largely land-
based tournament, they still optimistically hope to 
win and claim the conch of the depths: a legendary 
artifact they believe to be in Hao Jin’s vault that 
can command any ocean, even one on another 
plane, when sounded.

Thundering Tide vastly prefers to fight in the

unlikely to leave the water unless somehow forced 
to.  
 
DAY 2 
BOUGHS OF MITHRAL 
Named for the tree that is their nation’s symbol, 
this team of elves is from Jinin. Each of them are 
old enough that they were alive when Hao Jin was 
active and when she disappeared. Because of this, 
they recall an artifact Hao Jin placed in her vault 
that was forgotten by the rest of the world that 
they intend to claim should they win. They refuse 
to share any details beyond that.  
All team members are elves, have low-light vision, and increase 
their speed by 5 feet.

FANGS OF THE REMORHAZ 
A team from the Osman Confederation, in the icy 
Crown of the World, the Fangs of the Remorhaz 
are more dangerous than even their namesake, 
which each of them have slain before. They now 
seek a powerful weapon or allies to help defend 
their people from the ever-looming grasp of the 
frost giant Jarl Gnargorak.   
FANGS OF THE REMORHAZ (3) 
    CREATURE 12 
Weak Weapon Master 
Melee 
 longspear +26 [+21/+16] (magical, reach), Damage 
3d8+9 piercing 
Resistances cold 10 
The team employs a pincer formation not unlike 
the mandibles of a remorhaz. Their reach 
weapons allow them to take advantage of Dueling 
Expertise while several of them attack the same 
target or even flank, though you may wish to 
reflavor this ability as a cooperative hunting tactic 
or similar skill. They also use their reach and 
attack of opportunity to threat spellcasters and 
ranged attackers. 
 
MYTHSPEAKERS  
In the land of Iblydos in Casmaron, there exist 
individuals who straddle the line between divinity 
and mortality, known as hero-gods. Two such 
burgeoning hero-gods seek to build their own 
legends by participating in the Ruby Phoenix 
Tournament. Though they know Hao Jin holds a 
shield once used by another hero-god, their 
primary goal is to achieve feats and win battles 
worthy of legend.

KORADES 
 
 
    CREATURE 13 
Archery Specialist

Impossible Shots Korades’s arrows are imbued with his own 
divine will, and nothing can stop them from finding their marks. 
Korades’s Strikes with his longbow ignore all cover, 
concealment, and resistances.  
While allied, Akantha and Korades are after 
personal glory and engage in little cooperation. 
Akantha begins by barreling into the other team 
and using Knocking Sweep or attacking whichever 
foe strikes her as the strongest. Korades keeps his 
distance using his speed and shows off with 
Impossible Shots, almost never targeting the same 
foe as Akantha.  
 
PIERCE THE SKY 
This team of skilled gunslingers hails from the 
nation of Tazuni in the Deadshot Lands in 
Arcadia. Rumor has it that Hao Jin won a 
powerful weapon capable of piercing the sky in 
Arcadia, they believe this weapon to be one of the 
legendary Star Guns, and they intend to claim it 
from her vault.  
DEADSHOT GUNSLINGERS (3) 
    CREATURE 12 
Weak Archery Specialists, replace Pinning Shot, Point-Blank 
Shot, & Rain of Arrows 
Ranged 
 harmona gun +25 [+20/+15] (kickback, magical, 
range increment 150 feet, reload 1) Damage 3d10+6 
bludgeoning 
Mobile Sniper: 
 The gunslinger reloads while moving or 
using the terrain to their advantage. They Stride, Step, Sneak, 
Take Cover, or Hide, then Interact to reload. They must meet 
the requirements of these actions as normal. 
Utility Shot: 
 The gunslinger takes extra time to carefully 
line up a shot to disrupt their target’s plans. They Strike with 
their harmona gun against a target within its first range 
increment, and if it hits, in addition to dealing damage, the 
target is knocked prone, stunned 1, or pushed 10 feet 
backward. 
These gunslingers know they cannot match other 
teams in melee and seek to delay enemies sporting 
melee weapons from reaching them as long as 
possible. They accomplish this using Utility Shot, 
Mobile Sniper, careful assessment of the terrain, 
and by prioritizing enemy melee combatants.

GRASP OF FROST AND FLAME 
This pair of oni come from Chu Ye, a land where 
their kind rule. Still, they come in disguise as a 
frost and fire giant. These two come to the 
tournament not for treasure but for revenge: they 
have a deep rivalry with Koto Zekora, the top 
enforcer, and are especially incensed that she now 
serves humans.  
FIRE YAI 
 
 
    CREATURE 14 
ICE YAI  
 
 
    CREATURE 13 
In combat, the oni prefer to single out and double 
team one foe at a time, ideally flanking them. They 
have no reservations about using their innate 
spells and magical abilities, pretending to be ice 
and fire mages, but they cannot use their ice 
missile or fire missile Strikes in giant form. They 
begin by either blasting the enemy team with area 
attacks and then targeting the foe who seems most 
injured, or isolating a foe who seems particularly 
dangerous with wall spells.

the most powerful sorcerer in the world and hope

This team has access to an incredible range of 
spells, which allows them to adapt to nearly any 
situation, but also can be difficult to manage as a 
GM. The sorcerers are incredibly powerful 
magically, but have little tactical experience, 
especially as a team. If you feel up to it, you can 
have them rush into battle with little plan and 
decide which spells to use on the fly. If you don’t, 
select a few spells for each of them and play them 
as overly reliant on these spells.  
 
CRIMSON CLAWS 
Rumors abound about this team of Red Mantis 
Assassins’ goals in the tournament. Many believe 
they are here to assassinate a particular competitor 
or even an entire team, though others suggest that 
Hao Jin’s vaults may hold some relic sacred to 
Achaekek, and that she has allowed them to 
participate so that they have a chance of claiming 
it fairly.  
RED MANTIS ASSASSINS (2) 
    CREATURE 14 
Elite Agile Warrior, replace Deadly Disarm 
Melee 
 sawtooth saber +29 [+25/+21] (agile, finesse, 
magical, twin) Damage 2d6+11 slashing   
Prayer Attack 
 
The assassins use their speed and mobility to circle 
around opponents and attack their back rank, 
focusing especially on healers. They try to make 
every hit a sneak attack, using Prayer Attack, 
Tumbling Attack, flanking, or Stealth if possible, 
to make their enemies flat-footed. They use Step 
or Tumbling Attack to escape from enemy melee 
combatants.  
 
REACH OF THE HEAVENS 
This team of aasimar monks is from the celestially 
influenced nation of Tianjing. Each of them traces 
their descent from a different variety of celestial.  
If you wish, you can add the effect of a different 
aasimar lineage feat to each member of the team, 
but this adds significantly more detail to track and 
is unlikely to significantly impact a fight. The 
aasimars believe that if they can win the 
tournament that proves that they can take on an 
challenge, and will claim the mountain to the sky 
from Hao Jin’s vault, and ascend to Heaven to 
connect with their ancestors and seek a new quest 
there.  
AASIMAR MONKS (3) 
 
    CREATURE 13 
Ki Adept 
All are aasimars, have darkvision, and deal an additional 1 good 
damage on Strikes against evil creatures. 
Celestial Wings 
 
In combat, Reach of the Heavens display adept 
coordination. They are likely to delay their turns to 
all act in a row, so that one member can use 
Knocking Sweep or Knockdown while the others 
capitalize on the advantage with Flurry of Blows

CONSERVING SPELLS 
During Despair on Danger Island, other 
teams must conserve their spells & 
resources over many fights as well. A 
simple rule of thumb is to assume that 
opponents have full use of their focus 
spells, but have already used one spell 
of each level, unless it’s very early in 
the day. If it’s very late in the day, such 
as the fight against the Glowing 
Embers, assume opponents have used 
two spells of each level.  
 
PRE-BUFFING 
The rules surrounding casting 
preparatory spells in the tournament 
itself are not stated and are up to you 
to decide, but you should give the PCs

to allow spells that last longer than 1 
minute, as it usually takes about a 
minute for the combatants to get into 
position and the enforcer or announcer 
to introduce the fight.

NEW RULES & ITEMS 
This section contains changes and expansions to the performance combat rules presented in Ready? Fight! and the 
Chase subsystem used in Ready? Fight! and King of the Mountain. It also contains new items that can be used in the 
Fists of the Ruby Phoenix Adventure Path. 
THREE ACTION CHASES 
This variant on the standard Chase subsystem is designed to make 
them more engaging, especially for characters with few skills, and to 
mitigate the disappointment that comes with failing a check in a chase. 
It is important to note that playing with these rules does add more 
complexity and cause chases to take somewhat longer.   In this 
variant, characters in a chase have 3 actions per turn, as in a combat. 
Overcoming is a 2-action activity that otherwise functions as normal, 
so typically characters have one remaining action. The simplest way to 
account for the extra edge this grants characters is to raise the DCs of 
all obstacles by 1.  
     These rules work best in chases where a turn represents a 6-second 
combat round, so a character might use their action to Seek to notice 
details or Recall Knowledge  about who they are being pursued by or 
pursuing, to Cast a Spell like Guidance, or use other actions as 
appropriate to the situation. In longer chases where turns represent a 
minute or more, players may have to get creative, such as using a 
Summon spell and sustaining it for a minute to allow the summoned 
creature to make an Overcome check in addition to the summoner’s.  
     A good standby action that can be used over any period of time is 
Aid. Aid normally requires an action spent preparing and a reaction, 
but for the purposes of a chase you can waive the reaction. This also 
allows a character with no skills applicable to a particular obstacle to 
still participate by spending their turn Aiding or using other actions. 
The DC of the Aid action does not scale with level, which poses 
problems at low and high levels. Changing the DC to the Easy DC by 
level of the person being Aided or the DC of the check being Aided 
minus 5 are both excellent solutions.  
 
COMBAT CHASES 
Using this variant, chases can be fully integrated with combat, creating 
a running battle. This does require some use of theater of the mind, 
unless you really want to create a small map for each obstacle. In such 
a chase, characters can spend their actions advancing in the chase, 
participating in combat as normal, or some combination of both. For 
the purpose of targeting and range, creatures on the same obstacle 
should be considered 10 or fewer feet away and able to move adjacent 
to one another, creatures on the next or previous obstacle should be 
considered 30-60 feet away (GM’s discretion based on the specific 
chase), and creatures that are multiple obstacles apart generally cannot 
target each other due to the obstacles in the way. In a combat that 
starts as a chase, creatures can roll any of the skills used at the first 
obstacle for initiative.   
SOLO CHASES 
You can also run the chase rules such 
that each individual character moves 
separately. This is unlikely to occur in 
Fists of the Ruby Phoenix, as each 
chase occurs in a vehicle, but you 
might still find this variant useful for 
other campaigns or homebrew 
material. To do this, divide the number 
of chase points of each obstacle by 4 
(or divide it by 2 if characters are in 
pairs, etc.) To make it less likely that a 
character will be stuck on a particular 
obstacle, reduce the actions to 
Overcome an obstacle to 1, and require 
an action to Advance to the next 
obstacle. On a critical success to 
Overcome, a character may advance to 
the next obstacle as a free action, 
while on a critical failure, the 
character must spend their next action 
recovering from their mistake. Be 
wary if you use this style of chase to 
lead into a combat, as it can easily 
cause a character to become isolated 
and feel as though they are being 
punished for doing well in the chase.

DYNAMIC PERFORMANCE COMBAT 
These alternate rules are designed to create a 
performance combat system with more strategic 
depth, pulling rules from a combination of the 
performance combat rules from Ready? Fight!, 
Against the Scarlet Triad from the Age of Ashes 
Adventure Path, the performance combat rules 
from Pathfinder 1st edition, and the gladiator 
archetype. You can use these sources as 
inspiration if you want to modify these rules 
yourself or create your own.  
     When in a Performance Combat (any combat 
with a significant crowd of spectators), 
participants can roll Deception, Intimidation, 
Perception, or Performance for initiative. The 
crowd usually starts as neutral, with no bonuses to 
either side. Over the course of the fight, the 
participants can shift the attitude of the crowd to 
slightly or strongly favor one side or the other. A 
crowd that slightly favors a side grant that side a 
+1 status bonus to all checks (including attack 
rolls and saving throws) and weapon or unarmed 
damage rolls to that side, while a crowd that 
strongly favors a side grants a +2 bonus. At the 
GM’s discretion, the crowd may start out slightly 
favoring one side, or may award one participant 
with the opportunity to Play to the Crowd before 
combat starts.   
All participants gain the Play to the 
Crowd action. The DC to Play to the Crowd 
during the Ruby Phoenix Tournament is 35.  
Play to the Crowd 
 (auditory,  concentrate, emotion, visual) 
Requirements With your last action, you critically succeeded on 
an attack roll or skill check, or reduced a foe to 0 hp. At the 
GM’s discretion, a particularly impressive action may also allow 
you to use this action, such as a very flashy or effective spell. 
Effect With a mocking gesture, a triumphant flourish, or a bold 
challenge, you inspire the crowd to cheer you on. Attempt an 
Acrobatics, Athletics, Intimidation, or Performance check, with 
a DC set by the GM, based on the size of the crowd. Crowds 
grow bored with repetition though; and attempting to Play to 
the Crowd using the same skill that was used the last time 
someone used this action imposes a –2 circumstance penalty.  
Critical Success The crowd goes wild! You shift the crowd’s 
attitude towards your side by 2 steps, and until the end of your 
next turn, you have a status bonus 1 higher than the rest of your 
side. (This can give you a status bonus of +1 if the rest of your 
side has +0.) 
Success You appeal to the crowd. You shift the crowd’s attitude 
towards your side by 1 step. (Such as from neutral to slightly 
favoring or from slightly favoring to strongly) 
Failure You don’t make an impression.  
Critical Failure Your pandering is laughable, and the crowd 
begins to favor your opponents. You shift the crowd’s attitude 
one step towards your foes.  
 
TRACKING THE CROWD 
In order to help players remember these bonuses 
and the current state of the crowd, consider using 
a tracker like the one below.  
 
     If you play in person, you can clip the tracker 
to the front of your GM screen and use the clip to 
indicate the current bonus. If you play over a 
VTT, you can create a text box with the current 
bonus and place on the top and center of the 
battle map.  
 
GLADIATOR ARCHETYPE 
As the gladiator archetype was used as inspiration 
for the above performance combat rules, some of 
its feats are redundant. If you use the dynamic 
performance combat rules, make the following 
changes to the gladiator archetype: 
     Gladiator Dedication: When you roll 
Performance for initiative in a performance 
combat, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus.  
     Play to the Crowd: You can use the play to 
the crowd action as a reaction instead. You can 
choose to either sway the crowd toward your side 
or gain the normal benefits of the class feat. If you 
critically succeed when attempting to sway the 
crowd to your side, instead of gaining a status 
bonus 1 higher than the rest of your side, you can 
choose to gain one of the benefits of the feat (For 
example, you could shift the crowd’s attitude two 
steps toward your side and gain temporary hit 
points.) If you have the Call your Shot feat, you 
can choose that benefit.
